GENERAL SCIENCE — TERMLY EXAM #10
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: GENERAL SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 100 °C

2. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Overgrazing continuously

3. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. newton (N)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. joule (J)

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h.

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Response and coordination ● Types of nastic responses (haptonasty, chemonasty, t? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Response and coordination ● Types of nastic responses (haptonasty, chemonasty, t.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Response and coordination ● Types of nastic responses (haptonasty, chemonasty, t.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Response and coordination ● Types of nastic responses (haptonasty, chemonasty, t.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Response and coordination ● Types of nastic responses (haptonasty, chemonasty, t.

6. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Decomposers only
   B. Producers
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Tertiary consumers

7. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Human nervous system ● Components of the nervous system in a mammal (Central Ner? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Human nervous system ● Components of the nervous system in a mammal (Central Ner.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Human nervous system ● Components of the nervous system in a mammal (Central Ner.

   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Human nervous system ● Components of the nervous system in a mammal (Central Ner.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Thin Lenses 3.2 Newton’s Laws of Motion 3.3 Uniform Circular Motion 3.4 Heating ? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Thin Lenses 3.2 Newton’s Laws of Motion 3.3 Uniform Circular Motion 3.4 Heating .

   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Thin Lenses 3.2 Newton’s Laws of Motion 3.3 Uniform Circular Motion 3.4 Heating .

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Mole ● Relative Atomic Mass of elements ● Conversions of chemical quantities? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Mole ● Relative Atomic Mass of elements ● Conversions of chemical quantities.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Mole ● Relative Atomic Mass of elements ● Conversions of chemical quantities.

   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Transport in Animals ● Components of the human circulatory system ● The heart: s.

12. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. A mixture of two liquids

13. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

14. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Hydrocarbons ● Classification of hydrocarbons ● General formula and Nomenclature? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Hydrocarbons ● Classification of hydrocarbons ● General formula and Nomenclature.

----

18. In three clear sentences, explain Sensory and endocrine system in Human Beings ● The structure and functions of se and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Salts II ● Solubility of salts in water ● Factors affecting solubility of salts  and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
